message.content:
In this repository (/bench/repo), the "memos" server (Go), search for any GraphQL usage — grep for "graphql", "gqlgen", ".graphql" file extensions, "schema.graphql" across the entire repo, and check go.mod for GraphQL libraries. Also identify what the actual public API surface/protocol is (proto files under /bench/repo/proto/, gRPC/Connect-RPC services, REST gateway, etc.) and where the API schema/definitions actually live.

Report definitively: is GraphQL used anywhere in this codebase? If not, what is the actual API technology and where are its schema definitions located (file paths)?

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	package v1
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"net/http"
6	
7		"connectrpc.com/connect"
8		"github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/v2/runtime"
9		"github.com/labstack/echo/v5"
10		"golang.org/x/sync/semaphore"
11	
12		"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/markdown"
13		"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/profile"
14		v1pb "github.com/usememos/memos/proto/gen/api/v1"
15		"github.com/usememos/memos/server/auth"
16		"github.com/usememos/memos/server/notification"
17		"github.com/usememos/memos/store"
18	)
19	
20	const maxAPIRequestBytes = 256 << 20
21	
22	type APIV1Service struct {
23		v1pb.UnimplementedInstanceServiceServer
24		v1pb.UnimplementedAuthServiceServer
25		v1pb.UnimplementedUserServiceServer
26		v1pb.UnimplementedMemoServiceServer
27		v1pb.UnimplementedAttachmentServiceServer
28		v1pb.UnimplementedAIServiceServer
29		v1pb.UnimplementedShortcutServiceServer
30		v1pb.UnimplementedIdentityProviderServiceServer
31	
32		Secret                  string
33		Profile                 *profile.Profile
34		Store                   *store.Store
35		MarkdownService         markdown.Service
36		SSEHub                  *SSEHub
37		NotificationEmailSender notification.EmailSender
38	
39		// thumbnailSemaphore limits concurrent thumbnail generation to prevent memory exhaustion
40		thumbnailSemaphore       *semaphore.Weighted
41		imageProcessingSemaphore *semaphore.Weighted
42	
43		// instanceStatsCache memoizes GetInstanceStats results for instanceStatsCacheTTL.
44		instanceStatsCache instanceStatsCache
45	}
46	
47	func NewAPIV1Service(secret string, profile *profile.Profile, store *store.Store) *APIV1Service {
48		markdownService := markdown.NewService(
49			markdown.WithTagExtension(),
50			markdown.WithMentionExtension(),
51		)
52		return &APIV1Service{
53			Secret:                   secret,
54			Profile:                  profile,
55			Store:                    store,
56			MarkdownService:          markdownService,
57			SSEHub:                   NewSSEHub(),
58			NotificationEmailSender:  nil,
59			thumbnailSemaphore:       semaphore.NewWeighted(3), // Limit to 3 concurrent thumbnail generations
60			imageProcessingSemaphore: semaphore.NewWeighted(2),
61		}
62	}
63	
64	// RegisterGateway registers the gRPC-Gateway and Connect handlers with the given Echo instance.
65	func (s *APIV1Service) RegisterGateway(ctx context.Context, echoServer *echo.Echo) error {
66		// Shared authorizer: one source of truth for authentication and anonymous-access
67		// policy, used by both the gRPC-Gateway middleware and the Connect interceptor.
68		authorizer := NewAuthorizer(s.Store, s.Secret, s.Profile)
69		gatewayAuthMiddleware := func(next runtime.HandlerFunc) runtime.HandlerFunc {
70			return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, pathParams map[string]string) {
71				ctx := r.Context()
72	
73				// The RPC method name is set by grpc-gateway after routing. When it can't be
74				// determined, skip the policy check and let the service layer handle visibility.
75				rpcMethod, ok := runtime.RPCMethod(ctx)
76				authHeader := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
77	
78				result := authorizer.Authenticate(ctx, authHeader)
79				if ok {
80					if err := authorizer.CheckAccess(ctx, rpcMethod, result); err != nil {
81						http.Error(w, `{"code": 16, "message": "authentication required"}`, http.StatusUnauthorized)
82						return
83					}
84				}
85	
86				// Apply the identity to the context (no-op for permitted anonymous requests).
87				if result != nil {
88					r = r.WithContext(auth.ApplyToContext(ctx, result))
89				}
90	
91				next(w, r, pathParams)
92			}
93		}
94	
95		// Create gRPC-Gateway mux with auth middleware.
96		gwMux := runtime.NewServeMux(
97			runtime.WithMiddlewares(gatewayAuthMiddleware),
98		)
99		if err := v1pb.RegisterInstanceServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
100			return err
101		}
102		if err := v1pb.RegisterAuthServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
103			return err
104		}
105		if err := v1pb.RegisterUserServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
106			return err
107		}
108		if err := v1pb.RegisterMemoServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
109			return err
110		}
111		if err := v1pb.RegisterAttachmentServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
112			return err
113		}
114		if err := v1pb.RegisterAIServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
115			return err
116		}
117		if err := v1pb.RegisterShortcutServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
118			return err
119		}
120		if err := v1pb.RegisterIdentityProviderServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
121			return err
122		}
123		gwGroup := echoServer.Group("")
124		// Register SSE endpoint with same CORS as rest of /api/v1.
125		RegisterSSERoutes(gwGroup, s.SSEHub, s.Store, s.Secret)
126		handler := echo.WrapHandler(http.MaxBytesHandler(gwMux, maxAPIRequestBytes))
127	
128		gwGroup.Any("/api/v1/*", handler)
129		gwGroup.Any("/file/*", handler)
130	
131		// Connect handlers for browser clients (replaces grpc-web).
132		logStacktraces := s.Profile.Demo
133		connectInterceptors := connect.WithInterceptors(
134			NewMetadataInterceptor(), // Convert HTTP headers to gRPC metadata first
135			NewLoggingInterceptor(logStacktraces),
136			NewRecoveryInterceptor(logStacktraces),
137			NewAuthInterceptor(authorizer),
138		)
139		connectMux := http.NewServeMux()
140		connectHandler := NewConnectServiceHandler(s)
141		connectHandler.RegisterConnectHandlers(connectMux, connectInterceptors, connect.WithReadMaxBytes(maxAPIRequestBytes))
142	
143		connectGroup := echoServer.Group("")
144		connectGroup.Any("/memos.api.v1.*", echo.WrapHandler(http.MaxBytesHandler(connectMux, maxAPIRequestBytes)))
145	
146		return nil
147	}

I have a complete and definitive picture now.

## Answer: GraphQL is NOT used anywhere in this codebase

I searched exhaustively:
- `grep -ril "graphql"` across the entire repo (case-insensitive) → **zero matches**
- `grep -ril "gqlgen"` across the entire repo → **zero matches**
- `find . -iname "*.graphql"` → **zero files**
- `find . -iname "schema.graphql"` → **zero files**
- `go.mod` (and all transitive dependencies) → **no GraphQL library** (no `gqlgen`, `graphql-go`, `99designs/gqlgen`, etc.) referenced anywhere

## The actual API technology: gRPC + Protocol Buffers, exposed via grpc-gateway (REST/JSON) and Connect-RPC

This is a classic **protobuf-first** API design (buf-based), not GraphQL:

**Schema definitions (source of truth) — `/bench/repo/proto/`:**
- `proto/api/v1/` — the public API service definitions (protobuf `.proto` files):
  - `memo_service.proto`, `user_service.proto`, `auth_service.proto`, `attachment_service.proto`, `instance_service.proto`, `ai_service.proto`, `idp_service.proto`, `shortcut_service.proto`, `common.proto`
- `proto/store/` — internal storage-layer protobuf messages (`memo.proto`, `inbox.proto`, `idp.proto`, `instance_setting.proto`, `attachment.proto`, `user_setting.proto`)
- `proto/buf.yaml` and `proto/buf.gen.yaml` — buf build/codegen config, confirming this is a [buf](https://buf.build)-managed protobuf project

**Codegen plugins used (from `buf.gen.yaml`):**
- `protocolbuffers/go` — plain Go protobuf structs
- `grpc/go` — gRPC service stubs
- `connectrpc/go` — Connect-RPC handlers (`connect.com/connect`, used for browser clients, replacing grpc-web)
- `grpc-ecosystem/gateway` — grpc-gateway, which auto-generates a REST/JSON HTTP gateway from the same `.proto` service defs (via `google.api.http` annotations)
- `community/google-gnostic-openapi` — auto-generates an **OpenAPI 3.0** spec from the proto definitions, output to `proto/gen/openapi.yaml` (4057 lines) — this is the REST API's documentation artifact, itself derived from protobuf, not hand-written GraphQL/OpenAPI
- `bufbuild/es` — generates TypeScript/Connect-ES client code into `web/src/types/proto` for the frontend

**Generated code — `/bench/repo/proto/gen/`:**
- `proto/gen/api/v1/*.pb.go` — protobuf message types
- `proto/gen/api/v1/*_grpc.pb.go` — gRPC service stubs
- `proto/gen/api/v1/*.pb.gw.go` — grpc-gateway REST handlers
- `proto/gen/api/v1/apiv1connect/*.connect.go` — Connect-RPC handlers
- `proto/gen/openapi.yaml` — generated OpenAPI spec (for the REST surface)
- `proto/gen/store/*.pb.go` — internal store protobuf types

**Server wiring — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go`** (`RegisterGateway` method) shows all three transports being registered on the same Echo HTTP server:
1. grpc-gateway REST/JSON mux at `/api/v1/*` and `/file/*` (translates HTTP+JSON to gRPC calls, via `runtime.NewServeMux` from `github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/v2/runtime`)
2. Connect-RPC handlers at `/memos.api.v1.*` (using `connectrpc.com/connect`, for browser clients — explicitly noted in code comment as "replaces grpc-web")
3. Native gRPC service implementations underlying both

**go.mod confirms the stack** (no GraphQL deps present):
```
connectrpc.com/connect v1.19.2
github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/v2 v2.29.0
google.golang.org/grpc v1.80.0
```

**Bottom line:** memos' public API is defined entirely as Protocol Buffer service/message definitions under `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/*.proto` (and internal storage types under `/bench/repo/proto/store/*.proto`), compiled via buf into gRPC, Connect-RPC, and a REST/JSON gateway (with an auto-derived OpenAPI spec at `/bench/repo/proto/gen/openapi.yaml`). There is no GraphQL schema, resolver, gqlgen usage, or `.graphql` file anywhere in this repository.
